liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **Jam Session (musicians unknown)**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-10-31.sbd.bershaw.5416.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 1 songs; 9 min; rated 2.22/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the track is short, about five minutes, and the instrumental jam sounds excellent [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer guesses the performers may be a short-lived experimental group associated with Hendrix, not the Dead [3]
- Citing Tom Wolfe's book, reviewer says Anonymous Artists of America were to replace the Dead at a graduation, but left after military police kept interfering with sound [5]
- Reviewer says the Dead were advertised for a Halloween costume ball called Dance of Death at California Hall on Polk St [7]
- Reviewer says the performers are more likely the Anonymous Artists of America than the Grateful Dead [8]
- Self-described charter member of the band says they played Pomp and Circumstance at the Acid Test Graduation while Neal Cassidy handed out diplomas [9]
- Reviewer says guitar phrasing, bass line and fast tempo don't match the Dead of that era, who mixed electric blues and SF harmonies [4]
- Reviewer finds the jam too noisy to match the Dead, and thinks the Dead moved away from such sounds as the 1970s neared [6]
- Reviewer says the bass line shows this isn't the Dead; 1966 was the only 1960s Halloween falling on a Monday [7]
- Reviewer says the jam sounds unlike their band's Buchla-box synthesizer songs, none of which were instrumentals [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-10-31.sbd.bershaw.5416.shnf**: transferred by Alan Bershaw; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Taken from the compilation The Acid Test Reels 1965-1967, a chronological collection of Acid Test recordings listed in the Tapers Compendium Volume One [1]
